aboutUs.title: About Us
aboutUs.par1: The South Sudan Revenue Authority (Formerly National Revenue Authority) is the revenue service of the South Sudan Government; it is a non-oil Revenue collecting body that was established in 2016 under the National Revenue Authority Act, 2016. The South Sudan Revenue Authority branches include but are not limited to Domestic Tax division and Customs division.
aboutUs.branches: Parent Ministry: Ministry of Finance Jurisdiction: The Republic South Sudan

individualIntroductions.heading: Individual Taxpayer
individualIntroductions.intro: An individual taxpayer is any person who is liable for paying taxes. Any person having an income can be registered as a taxpayer. This applies to South Sudanese nationals, residents and non-residents whose source of income is in South Sudan.

indFaqs.head: Is there a penalty for non-compliance?
indFaqs.body: Penalties and additional charges will be applied according to the Taxation Act Sections 36, 37 and 38 on late payments and filing.

indFaqs.head: What happens if I do not file my returns before the deadline?
indFaqs.body: Penalty charges of 5% shall be counted till the day the payment is executed.

indFaqs.head: Who has access to my tax information?
indFaqs.body: Tax information is confidential. Unless authorized by law, no person has the right to request the taxation department for information of tax other than his/her personal information or tax information of a business in which he/she is a partner.

indFaqs.head: Can my TIN expire?
indFaqs.body: The TIN issued to an individual cannot expire but it can be canceled, in a situation where an individual dies, or if the legal status of a person changes, if a person was registered in error, or if there is any other cases legally accepted by the laws of South Sudan

taxAppBsns.title: Taxes that apply to Businesses
taxAppBsns.heading: Business profit tax
taxAppBsns.intro: Business profit tax is an indirect tax charged on the taxable profit (Net profit) on the percentages prescribed in Schedule 1 of the Taxation Act of 2019/2020.

taxAppBsns.title: Taxes that apply to Businesses
taxAppBsns.heading: Withholding tax
taxAppBsns.intro: This is a method where the payer of certain incomes is responsible for deducting tax at source from payments made. The deducted tax must be remitted to the NRA. Withholding tax is meant to be filed on a specific date.

taxAppBsns.title: Taxes that apply to Businesses
taxAppBsns.heading: Advance Tax
taxAppBsns.intro: Advance tax is an indirect tax charged based on the projected net profit of a business per quarter. This is then reconciled annually. Taxpayers shall remit an advance payment of tax in an amount prescribed by regulation on or before the following dates;

taxAppBsns.title: Taxes that apply to Businesses
taxAppBsns.heading: Excise tax
taxAppBsns.intro: Excise duty is a tax imposed on goods and services manufactured in South Sudan or imported into South Sudan. This is an indirect tax which is included in the selling price of excisable goods and specific services. Excise tax is specified generally but is based on the goods or item multiplied by the individual excisable services according to Schedule 1 of the Financial Act of 2019/2020.

dedAndDeps.intro: Based on section 75 intangible property which has limited life i.e. including patents, copyrights, licenses for drawings and models, contracts and franchises, are deductible according to their useful life from amortization charges as determined by regulation.

bsnFaqs.head: What happens is I do not file my returns before the deadline?
bsnFaqs.body: Penalty charges of 5% shall be counted till the day the payment is executed.

bsnFaqs.head: Can I apply for an extension on the filing deadline?
bsnFaqs.body: Yes, as long as the taxpayer applies for the extension before the last day of payment, he/she can be granted 2 months to file the returns.

bsnFaqs.head: Who has access to my tax information?
bsnFaqs.body: Tax information are confidential, unless authorized by law, no person has the right to request the taxation department for information of tax other than his/her personal information or tax information of a business in which he/she is a partner,

bsnFaqs.head: What if the deadline for filing is not a business day?
bsnFaqs.body: If the deadline for filing the tax is not a business working day the following business day shall be considered to be the deadline, though granting the extension of filing date does not suspend the accrual of interest.

bsnFaqs.head: What is considered to be imported goods?
bsnFaqs.body: All goods brought or entered into South Sudan are considered imported goods and shall be subject to an advance payment of business profit tax, excise tax and general sales tax or otherwise as the goods may be categorized.

bsnFaqs.head: What should I do to be exempted from tax as a contractor?
bsnFaqs.body: Certificate of exemption is issued by the minister of finance, therefore if a foreign contractor is exempted from business profit tax he/she should present the certificate of exemption.

invIntros.title: Introduction
invIntros.heading: Investment in South Sudan
invIntros.intro: South Sudan has developed strong growth prospects supported by flourishing peace, rising levels of literacy and increasing opportunities for business. As the youngest nation in the world, South Sudan is open for business to companies, organizations and businesses seeking the strategic opportunity of tapping into the potential of a fast emerging market in Africa.
invIntros.content1: Great opportunities exist in South Sudan's natural resources, including but not limited to oil, precious metals and gum arabica. South Sudan offers a rich cultural experience and a vast wealth of natural attractions including the majestic white Nile. Gain insight into the many diverse and fascinating cultures found in the country—presenting endless opportunities for the tourism industry.
invIntros.content2: Both fiscal and non-fiscal incentives are available in South Sudan. The National Revenue Authority implements the issuance of tax incentives in collaboration with other regulators and facilitators such as the Ministry of Investment.
